title.en: Runners take on 'world's coolest marathon' on drifting North Pole ice
title.zh: 跑者在漂浮的北极冰面上挑战“世界上最酷的马拉松”

summary.en: Organisers reported that 23 runners from seven countries participated in races held at the geographic North Pole in the Arctic.
summary.zh: 组织者称，来自七个国家的23名跑者参加了在北极地理北极点举行的比赛。

body.en:
Twenty-three runners from seven countries took part in races at the Arctic's geographic North Pole, organisers have said, in an event they dubbed as the "world's coolest marathon".

The races took place on drifting sea ice at the geographic North Pole in the Arctic, with competitors arriving from Norway aboard the French polar vessel Le Commandant Charcot.

They disembarked the ship to run laps of a 1,055 metre loop on the ice below, wearing thermal gear and life vests as a safety requirement, while armed guards kept watch for polar bears around the perimeter.

Denmark's Rikke Dam won the women's title with a time of 6:54:02 and Wang Shengxian of China won the men's race in 3:52:22. Organisers said the course disappeared with the ice just hours after the races ended.
body.zh: 组织者表示，来自七个国家的 23 名跑步者参加了在北极地区举行的比赛，他们将这场比赛称为“世界上最酷的马拉松”。 比赛在北极地理北极的漂流海冰上举行，参赛者乘坐法国极地船 Le Commandant Charcot 从挪威抵达。 为了安全起见，他们下了船，在冰层上绕了 1,055 米长的圈，穿着保暖装备和救生衣，而武装警卫则在周围监视着北极熊。 丹麦选手里克·达姆以6小时54分02秒的成绩获得女子组冠军，中国选手王胜贤以3小时52分22秒的成绩获得男子组冠军。组织者表示，比赛结束几小时后，赛道就随着结冰消失了。

reflection.en: The dedication of these athletes, pushing their limits in an extreme environment, reflects the discipline required to pursue any challenging goal. While their achievement earns a remarkable, yet perishable, recognition, it reminds us of the deeper pursuit for an imperishable crown that transcends earthly accolades.
reflection.zh: 这些运动员在极端环境中挑战极限的奉献精神，反映了追求任何具有挑战性目标所需的纪律。虽然他们的成就赢得了非凡但终将消逝的荣誉，但这提醒我们，更深层的追求是那超越世俗赞誉的永不朽坏的冠冕。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Ferry carrying 116 passengers sinks off Guyana coast, authorities say
title.zh: 当局称，载有116名乘客的渡轮在圭亚那海岸附近沉没

summary.en: Authorities report that a ferry carrying 116 passengers has sunk off the coast of Guyana, with eight passengers rescued so far after the vessel capsized between Georgetown and Port Kaituma.
summary.zh: 当局称，一艘载有116名乘客的渡轮在圭亚那海岸附近沉没，该船在乔治敦和凯图马港之间倾覆后，目前已有八名乘客获救。

body.en:
A ferry carrying 116 passengers has sunk off the coast of Guyana with 53 people so far rescued, local authorities have said.

The MV Barima capsized near Iron Punt, on its route from the capital Georgetown to Port Kaituma on Saturday.

A distress call was received at 23:01 local time (03:01GMT), triggering a search operation involving state and private boats, Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said in a statement posted on social media.

"There is an active search and rescue operation that is taking place, and we pray for the safety of all," Edghill said on Sunday, AFP news agency reports.

Emergency teams expect to find more survivors as operations continue, Guyana Prime Minister Mark Phillips told AFP. He added that those rescued so far include both passengers and crew.

Three assistance centres have been set up for relatives of those rescued and passengers still missing, Phillips said on Facebook.

The names of those onboard will be released once rescue operations and medical checks are complete, he added.

The MV Barima was built in 1939 and is 40m (131ft) long, according to a listing on VesselFinder.

Edghill said it was fitted with 250 life jackets, two rigid life crafts and six inflatable life crafts.

title.en: Fact check: Spotting AI-generated 'historical' images
title.zh: 事实核查：发现人工智能生成的“历史”图像

summary.en: DW Fact check selected three "historical" videos that aren't real — they're AI. Could you recognize the fake? Here's how to spot it — and why it matters.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 德国之声事实调查选择了三个不真实的“历史”视频——它们是人工智能。你能认出假货吗？以下是如何发现它以及它为何如此重要。 在意大利庞贝古城，考古学家首次利用人工智能重建了公元 79 年火山喷发受害者的图像。 随着人工智能技术的广泛应用，人工智能越来越多地被用来生成“历史”图像，而且大多不需要专家的咨询。 苏黎世大学媒体学者罗兰·迈耶 (Roland Meyer) 认为这一趋势并非巧合。 他说：“通过人工智能，似乎可以重新组合过去的图像，生成不存在但可能存在的合成图像，从而填补档案和历史记录中感知或实际的空白。” “然而，对我来说，这似乎是一个欺骗性的承诺。” 众所周知，人工智能生成器会犯错误并产生“幻觉”。 DW 事实核查解释了如何发现 AI 创建的“历史”视频。 许多病毒式传播的人工智能生成的“历史”视频声称展示了过去，模糊了事实与娱乐之间的界限。通常只需询问视频是否可以制作，就可以识别出他们。 “我们是在谈论视频已经存在的时代，还是在视频不存在的时代？”历史学家兼人工智能专家 Sebastian Kubon 问道。 这段据称描绘庞贝古城的视频仅凭这一点就可以被怀疑。 它还显示出人工智能生成的明显迹象。人们的动作就像僵尸一样，而女人的外表看起来比我们所知道的古罗马要现代得多。 人工智能工具的兴起使得创建此类“历史”图像和视频变得比以往任何时候都容易，但专家警告说，人工智能是根据现有数据进行训练的，并且会重复其偏见。 迈耶说：“人工智能生成的过去图像主要再现了迄今为止描绘过去的典型模式、陈词滥调和刻板印象。” “最重要的是，这些是我们期望的图像：不是了解过去的窗口，而是我们现在的镜子。” 其次，仔细研究图像本身及其来源是有帮助的。 在这段视频中，镜头滑近一群举着美国国旗的士兵，露出他们凝视远方的脸。它看起来更像是一部好莱坞电影，而不是真实的纪录片片段。 背景中的一名士兵出现了不自然的故障。水印也暴露了这一点：该视频是由生成式人工智能工具 Veo 制作的。 上述视频取材于 1945 年硫磺岛美军士兵的标志性照片。没有具体的真实视频片段......

title.en: US and Iran trade fire after two US soldiers killed in Jordan
title.zh: 美国和伊朗在两名美军士兵在约旦遇害后交换打击

summary.en: US forces have targeted Iranian sites for the eighth consecutive night, following an attack that killed two US soldiers in Jordan. Iran has responded by claiming it fired drones at US military targets in Kuwait, marking an escalation in regional tensions.
summary.zh: 在两名美国士兵在约旦遇害后，美军已连续第八晚袭击伊朗目标。伊朗则声称向科威特境内的美军发射了无人机，标志着地区紧张局势的升级。

body.en:
The US and Iran have exchanged strikes for an eighth consecutive day, after an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan killed two US soldiers and left another missing.

Iranian media said an under-construction nuclear power plant in the south-western city of Darkhoveyn had been struck overnight, as well as Qeshm Island. In Kuwait an electricity and water plant was hit for a second time, local officials said.

Later on Sunday three Iranian missiles were shot down by Jordan's military, and a fourth fell in a remote area, Jordan's state news agency said. It followed a US warning that the Jordanian port of Aqaba could be targeted.

The US and Iran have ramped up attacks against each other in recent days, with both sides accused of striking critical infrastructure.

Washington has also reimposed its blockade of Iranian ports and Tehran has declared the Strait of Hormuz - a key oil shipping route - closed, as their preliminary ceasefire collapsed less than a month after it began.

On Sunday, the IRGC said two vessels had ignored Iranian warnings not to transit the Strait and were consequently involved in "an accident". It warned that all vessels that are "influenced" by the US and "use unsafe routes" will "certainly face accidents".

The US military said its eighth successive night of attacks on Iran were "designed to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz" and "swiftly punish Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces who launched attacks against American service members in Jordan last night".

Verified footage from inside the Jordanian facility showed at least two impacts and an explosion.

Responding to the deaths of US soldiers, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said: "Godspeed, heroes. Their sacrifice only stiffens our resolve."

The US death toll in the conflict has now risen to 16 after an American Navy pilot who went missing earlier this month was declared dead.

In Iran, at least 50 people have been killed and more than 500 injured in US strikes over the past three weeks, the country's health ministry says.

On Saturday the Gulf Cooperation Council - an alliance including Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates - accused Tehran of targeting civilian infrastructure after the first strike on a Kuwaiti power plant and a water distillation plant.

On Sunday, Kuwait said the same power and water distillation plant had been hit for the second time by Iran in two days, resulting in a fire.

Iran said it had also targeted an air base and a depot used by US forces in Kuwait on Saturday.

The US has meanwhile said it "carried out strikes exclusively on military targets, including military logistics infrastructure" after Iran said bridges and a station were hit.

body.zh: 美国军方官员表示，美国周六晚间对伊朗发动了新一轮空袭，目标是其沿海监视和防空设施。 美国中央司令部（Centcom）表示，部队成功打击了伊朗的军事能力，而伊朗官方媒体则表示，霍尔木兹海峡的格什姆岛已遭到袭击。 中央司令部表示，它还针对伊朗革命卫队（IRGC），该组织对周五在约旦造成两名美军死亡的袭击负责，另一名军人仍然失踪。 据官方媒体报道，作为对最新袭击的回应，伊朗军队表示，他们对科威特的两个美国基地进行了无人机袭击。 最近几天，美国和伊朗加大了对对方的攻击力度，双方都被指控袭击了关键基础设施。 据伊朗革命卫队下属的塔斯尼姆通讯社报道，伊朗周六表示，它对美国“乌代里营”军事基地和“科威特阿里萨勒姆空军基地”的另一个军事基地进行了“大规模袭击”。 美国中央司令部表示，美国连续第八晚发动袭击，“旨在进一步削弱伊朗威胁霍尔木兹海峡商业航运的能力”。 声明继续说，这次袭击是为了“迅速惩罚昨晚在约旦对美国军人发动袭击的伊斯兰革命卫队部队”。 此前一周，敌对行动再次爆发，华盛顿重新封锁伊朗港口，德黑兰宣布关闭霍尔木兹海峡，初步停火在开始不到一个月后就破裂了。 美国中央司令部在周六早些时候的一份声明中表示：“在美国中央司令部和伙伴部队防御伊朗弹道导弹和无人机袭击的行动中，两名驻扎在约旦的美国军人丧生。此外，目前还有一名军人失踪。” 美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 在 X 上发帖回应死亡事件，称：“英雄们，祝你好运。他们的牺牲只会坚定我们的决心。” 本月早些时候失踪的一名美国海军飞行员被宣布死亡，美国在冲突中的死亡人数现已上升至 16 人，这是本周死亡人数第二次增加。 伊朗卫生部表示，过去三周美国的空袭已造成伊朗至少 50 人死亡、500 多人受伤。 美国和伊朗都被指控以民用基础设施为目标。美国否认了这一说法，称在伊朗称桥梁和车站遭到袭击后，美国“专门针对军事目标进行了打击，包括军事后勤基础设施”。 周六，海湾合作委员会指责德黑兰以民用基础设施为目标，此前科威特称一座发电厂和一座水蒸馏设施......

reflection.en: The ongoing exchange of strikes between nations tragically illustrates the ancient warning that violence often begets more violence. In such cycles, the path of retaliation can lead to deeper conflict and suffering for all involved. Yahweh calls us to seek ways to break these destructive patterns.
reflection.zh: 国家之间持续的交火悲剧性地印证了古老的警示，即暴力往往会滋生更多的暴力。在这样的循环中，报复的道路可能导致更深的冲突和所有相关方的痛苦。雅伟呼召我们寻求打破这些破坏性模式的方法。

title.en: What happened to Nolan Wells? Family seeks answers two weeks after 18-year-old’s death
title.zh: 诺兰·威尔斯发生了什么？18岁少年去世两周后，家人仍在寻求答案

summary.en: An investigation is ongoing into the death of 18-year-old college freshman Nolan Wells, who was found dead on a Mississippi island two weeks after a boat trip with friends. His family continues to search for answers regarding his passing.
summary.zh: 18岁的大学新生诺兰·威尔斯在一次与朋友的船上旅行后，被发现死于密西西比州的一个岛屿上。两周后，调查仍在进行中，他的家人仍在寻求关于他去世的答案。

body.en:
Two weeks after Nolan Xavier Wells was found dead, his family is still searching for answers.

On 4 July, Wells, an 18-year-old Mississippi college freshman, and a group of friends took a boat out to Horn Island, a barrier island a few miles off the Mississippi Gulf coast.

About 300 young adults gathered on a section of the island for a “last hurrah” before returning to college or work, one of Wells’s friends said. Wells’s parents were supposed to take him to Southwest Mississippi Community College for football camp the following Monday.

Wells’s friends, his phone and his keys returned that day; he did not. Instead, after a missing person search that received national attention, his body was found on the island on 6 July.

What exactly happened on Horn Island is still unclear, as is how the Ocean Springs native died; an investigation by local officials is ongoing. In the absence of answers, misinformation, particularly on social media, is rampant. Here’s what we know so far.

Late on 4 July, a Facebook post by Christine Wonsley, Wells’s mother, in which she sought answers about her then missing son, went viral .

When she shared a photo of Wells, who was Black, and three friends, who are white, social media users began suggesting that whatever happened to Wells was racially motivated.

At a press conference on 10 July in New York, after Wells’s body was found, Wonsley addressed the racial nature of the situation.

“Me and his dad had conversations with him all the time, not just about the importance of understanding our history as Black people, but also the importance of how you have to move in certain spaces,” she said, standing by the Rev Al Sharpton and Ben Crump, who the family has retained as an attorney.

Crump said on Sunday at the New Birth Missionary Baptist church outside Atlanta: “We are in Mississippi. These were three young white men. Nolan was the only young Black man. Had the roles been reversed, we know this investigation would be going differently. It would be like the first 48. They would be interrogating those young, Black boys.”

Ashlee Cole, the mother of one of Wells’s white friends and a Jackson county chancery judge, denied that her family had hindered the investigation in a statement. She said that her son had been interviewed by the Jackson county sheriff’s office and alleged that Wells left the island with a separate group of friends.

Tracestin Shepherd, who said he was a friend of Wells and was on the island on 4 July, told ABC News that Wells met a young woman and wanted to stay behind. Crump has said that the young woman said Wells decided to return with his friends. Horn Island is a designated wilderness area. It’s undeveloped, except for a small ranger station, and has neither utilities nor a commercial ferry...
body.zh: 诺兰·泽维尔·威尔斯被发现死亡两周后，他的家人仍在寻找答案。 7 月 4 日，18 岁的密西西比大学新生威尔斯和一群朋友乘船前往霍恩岛，这是距离密西西比湾海岸几英里的一座障壁岛。 威尔斯的一位朋友说，大约 300 名年轻人在返回大学或工作之前聚集在岛上的一个地区进行“最后的欢呼”。威尔斯的父母本应在下周一带他去西南密西西比社区学院参加橄榄球训练营。 那天，威尔斯的朋友、他的手机和钥匙都回来了；他没有。相反，在一次引起全国关注的失踪人员搜寻之后，他的尸体于 7 月 6 日在岛上被发现。 霍恩岛上究竟发生了什么，以及这位海泉市当地人是如何死亡的，目前仍不清楚。当地官员正在进行调查。在缺乏答案的情况下，错误信息（尤其是社交媒体上的错误信息）十分猖獗。这是我们目前所知道的。 7 月 4 日晚，威尔斯母亲克里斯汀·旺斯利 (Christine Wonsley) 在 Facebook 上发布的一条帖子在网上疯传，她在帖子中寻求有关她当时失踪的儿子的答案。 当她分享了一张黑人威尔斯和三个白人朋友的照片时，社交媒体用户开始暗示，发生在威尔斯身上的一切都是出于种族动机。 7 月 10 日，在纽约举行的新闻发布会上，威尔斯的尸体被发现后，旺斯利谈到了这一情况的种族性质。 “我和他的父亲一直在与他交谈，不仅讨论了解我们作为黑人的历史的重要性，还讨论在某些空间中如何移动的重要性，”她站在阿尔·夏普顿牧师和本·克伦普的身边说，他们的家人聘请了他们担任律师。 克伦普周日在亚特兰大郊外的新生传教士浸信会教堂说：“我们在密西西比州。这是三名年轻的白人。诺兰是唯一的年轻黑人。如果角色互换，我们知道这次调查将会有所不同。就像前 48 次一样。他们会审问那些年轻的黑人男孩。” 阿什莉·科尔（Ashlee Cole）是威尔斯一位白人朋友的母亲，也是杰克逊县法官，她在一份声明中否认她的家人阻碍了调查。她说，她的儿子接受了杰克逊县治安官办公室的约谈，并声称威尔斯与另一群朋友离开了该岛。 特雷斯汀·谢泼德 (Tracestin Shepherd) 自称是威尔斯的朋友，7 月 4 日就来到了岛上，他告诉美国广播公司新闻，威尔斯遇到了一位年轻女子，并想留下来。克伦普说，这名年轻女子说威尔斯决定和他的朋友一起回来。霍恩岛是指定的荒野地区。它尚未开发，除了一个小型护林站外，既没有公用设施，也没有商业渡轮……

reflection.en: The profound grief of a family seeking answers after a sudden, unexplained loss is a heavy burden. In such moments, the shortest verse in the Bible reminds us that Yahweh understands our sorrow, for "Jesus wept" at the tomb of a friend. This simple truth affirms that tears are a natural and sacred response to the pain of loss, and we are not alone in our...
reflection.zh: 一个家庭在突如其来的、不明原因的丧失后寻求答案，这种深切的悲痛是沉重的负担。在这样的时刻，圣经中最短的经文提醒我们，雅伟理解我们的悲伤，因为“耶稣哭了”在他朋友的墓前。这个简单的真理肯定了眼泪是对失落之痛的自然而神圣的回应，我们并非独自承受痛苦。

verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: EU ban on destroying unsold clothes takes effect
title.zh: 欧盟禁止销毁未售出衣服的禁令生效

summary.en: Under new rules to reduce waste, large companies across the European Union can no longer dispose of unsold clothes, accessories and footwear.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Under new rules to reduce waste, large companies across the European Union can no longer dispose of unsold clothes, accessories and footwear.

A ban on the disposal of unsold clothes and shoes took effect across the European Union on Sunday, in the bloc's latest move to cut waste.

Hundreds of thousands of tons of fashionwear are destroyed every year across the 27-member EU due to damage, old stock and returned online orders.

The new rule is expected to affect large fashion retailers, wholesalers and manufacturers of apparel — only 20% of which are produced in the EU.

Under the EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, large companies with more than 250 employees and over €50 million in net annual turnover are banned from destroying stocks of unsold clothing, accessories and footwear.

Firms must now find ways of selling the products, including via discounts, alternative markets and charity donations.

Unsold clothes can only be destroyed when items are unsafe, damaged, counterfeit or rejected by charities, according to a post on the European Commission's website.

Companies are now required to publish annual reports on the goods they have discarded and keep records for five years.

The regulation, which was approved by Brussels more than two years ago, will be extended to medium-sized firms in 2030.

Concerns about so-called fast fashion — low-cost, lower-quality mass-produced clothing — have grown significantly over the past decade.

According to the European Environment Agency (EEA), around 4% to 9% of unsold textile products are destroyed each year.

Across the EU, one in five fashion goods ordered online is later returned to the retailer and not resold.

Combined, this amounts to hundreds of thousands of tons of clothes, accessories and footwear.

The new ban aims to help reduce the impact on the environment , as the incineration of millions of clothes hits efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions.

EU states are also under pressure to consider waste from raw materials, water, energy and transport in the apparel sector and to encourage more recycling and the reuse of products.

In a recent LinkedIn post, the EEA said the bloc wanted the textile industry to become more sustainable.

"A circular economy — where products are designed to last, and are reused, repaired and recycled — is no longer just a vision, but is being embedded in law through these new legislative measures," the EEA wrote.

The fashion industry has repeatedly defended its tactics, noting that disposal is often cheaper than storing, repairing or discounting the products.

body.zh: 根据减少浪费的新规定，欧盟各地的大公司不能再处理未售出的衣服、配饰和鞋类。 周日，欧盟范围内禁止处理未售出的衣服和鞋子的禁令生效，这是欧盟减少浪费的最新举措。 在欧盟 27 个成员国中，每年有数十万吨时装因损坏、旧库存和网上订单退货而被销毁。 新规定预计将影响大型时装零售商、批发商和服装制造商——其中只有 20% 是在欧盟生产的。 根据欧盟可持续产品生态设计法规，员工超过 250 名、年净营业额超过 5000 万欧元的大公司被禁止销毁未售出的服装、配饰和鞋类库存。 企业现在必须找到销售产品的方式，包括通过折扣、替代市场和慈善捐赠。 根据欧盟委员会网站上的一篇文章，只有当物品不安全、损坏、伪造或被慈善机构拒绝时，未售出的衣服才会被销毁。 现在，公司必须公布其丢弃的货物的年度报告，并保存记录五年。 该法规于两年多前获得布鲁塞尔批准，将于 2030 年扩展到中型企业。 过去十年，人们对所谓的快时尚（低成本、低质量的批量生产服装）的担忧显着增长。 根据欧洲环境署 (EEA) 的数据，每年约有 4% 至 9% 的未售出纺织品被销毁。 在整个欧盟，网上订购的时尚商品有五分之一随后被退回零售商而不是转售。 加起来，这相当于数十万吨的衣服、配饰和鞋类。 新禁令旨在帮助减少对环境的影响，因为焚烧数百万件衣服会影响减少温室气体排放的努力。 欧盟国家还面临压力，需要考虑服装行业中原材料、水、能源和运输产生的废物，并鼓励更多的产品回收和再利用。 在最近的 LinkedIn 帖子中，欧洲经济区表示，该集团希望纺织业变得更加可持续。 欧洲经济区写道：“循环经济——产品的设计经久耐用，并可重复使用、修理和回收——不再只是一个愿景，而是通过这些新的立法措施被纳入法律。” 时尚界一再为其策略辩护，指出处理产品通常比储存、修理或打折产品便宜。 德国零售联合会（HDE）表示，随着更多……消费者将从禁令中受益。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: Influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate arrested in US on new charges, face extradition
title.zh: 网红安德鲁·泰特和特里斯坦·泰特在美国因新指控被捕，面临引渡

summary.en: Influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate have been arrested in the US on new charges and are now facing extradition to the United Kingdom.
summary.zh: 知名网红安德鲁·泰特和特里斯坦·泰特在美国因新指控被捕，目前正面临被引渡到英国。

body.en:
Radical social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate have been arrested in the United States as British authorities seek their extradition on rape and sex trafficking charges.

The brothers' social media empire promoting wealth, male dominance and misogyny has made them among the world's most polarising internet personalities.

The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrest of 39-year-old Andrew Tate, a self-professed misogynist, and his younger brother on a sealed warrant, placing the US at the centre of an international legal saga that has stretched from Romania to Britain.

US news outlet TMZ posted a video of law enforcement officers placing the men in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles. Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on social media platform X showed.

British prosecutors said on Sunday they were prosecuting Andrew Tate with seven further counts of rape, three counts of facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault and 19 additional charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. He has already been charged previously for 10 counts of rape, assault and human trafficking.

Tristan Tate had been charged with an six more counts of sexual assault, rape and facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. He already has 11 previous charges for the same crimes.

British prosecutors seeking the brothers' extradition alleging they conducted these offences between 2010 and 2017.

They were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations and the case didn't go forward because of legal and procedural irregularities.

The pending charges in the United Kingdom accused the brothers of abusing women in an area north of London, where they grew up. Their lawyers had said they denied the allegations.

Joseph McBride, a lawyer representing the Tate brothers, said in a phone interview he had not been able to speak with his clients but called the new charges out of the UK "filth and slander" intended to derail defamation lawsuits filed by the brothers in the US.

"They're pulling out all the stops to make sure these guys never get their day in court," McBride said.

"We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free. America does not do Britain's political dirty work."

title.en: United States launches new strikes on Iran after two US soldiers killed by Iranian attack
title.zh: 两名美国士兵被伊朗袭击身亡后，美国对伊朗发动新一轮袭击

summary.en: The United States has launched new strikes on Iran following an Iranian attack that killed two US soldiers. This escalation has led to further casualties, with both nations continuing to target the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 在伊朗袭击导致两名美国士兵死亡后，美国对伊朗发动了新的袭击。此次升级导致更多生命逝去，两国再次将目标对准霍尔木兹海峡。

body.en:
The United States said it had completed an eighth straight night of attacks against Iran after earlier announcing that two US military personnel were killed in Jordan and another was missing following an Iranian attack.

The US and Iran have intensified ‌attacks since an interim ceasefire deal signed a month ago fell apart last week, raising the possibility of a return to all-out war.

US Central Command said in a statement that the strikes were "designed to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and swiftly punish Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces who launched attacks against American service members in Jordan last night".

Central Command later said it had completed its wave of attacks, hitting Iranian military coastal surveillance and air defence facilities.

Iran's Mehr news agency said the US carried out an attack near Sirik in southern Iran, adding that no casualties or damage to infrastructure have been reported. The Tasnim news agency said the US military also targeted a location near Shadegan, close to the border with Iraq.

The Iranian army then carried out a drone attack that targeted US military assets and equipment at Kuwait's Al-Adiri camp and Ali Al Salem Air Base, Iran's state TV reported early Sunday, citing a statement from the army.

Both bases were targeted as part of Iran's attacks against US assets and allies in the Gulf since last week.

Central Command said the two deaths occurred on Friday and that a third US service member was missing in action. The announcement brought the number of US service members killed since the war began to 16, while more than 420 have been wounded.

US defence secretary Pete Hegseth posted on X: "Godspeed, heroes. Their sacrifice only stiffens our resolve."

Iran, responding to US attacks on bridges, power facilities and other infrastructure, appeared to target Saudi Arabia as well as other US Gulf allies and Jordan on Saturday.

In a written statement carried by the official social media accounts of Iran's supreme leader and Iranian state media, Mojtaba Khamenei said repeated US breaches of the interim deal had shown that President Donald Trump's signature was "utterly worthless and devoid of credibility".

"Now that the American enemy is seeking to escalate the conflict thereby incurring even heavier costs and further humiliation, it should know that ‌the noble nation of Iran ‌and the Resistance Front have unforgettable lessons ⁠in store for it," the statement said.

title.en: China firm seeks damages over state control of British Steel
title.zh: 中国公司就英国钢铁国有化寻求赔偿

summary.en: China's Jingye Group is seeking compensation from the UK government after the government took over British Steel last year. The UK government intervened to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility, which Jingye Group had purchased in 2020.
summary.zh: 中国敬业集团正向英国政府寻求赔偿，此前英国政府去年接管了英国钢铁公司，以防止该国最后一个主要炼钢设施关闭。敬业集团于2020年收购了该公司。

body.en:
The UK government took over British Steel last year to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility. China's Jingye Group, which bought the firm in 2020, claims it is owed compensation.

A Chinese steel giant demanded compensation from the United Kingdom   government on Sunday, claiming the state's takeover of its subsidiary, British Steel, was "outright robbery."

The UK government took operational control of British Steel last year, after owner Jingye Group warned that Britain's last factory capable of making steel from scratch was no longer financially viable.

In a statement on social media on Saturday, Jingye threatened legal action against the UK government, accusing ministers of "trampling on international investment rules."

Describing the nationalization as "outright robbery," the Chinese firm said it "reserves all legal rights, firmly defends its lawful rights and interests, and will pursue full compensation through legal means to the very end."

"The UK disregarded Jingye's continuous investment and significant contribution and was only willing to provide almost zero compensation,” the statement continued.

The company noted that nationalization could cost UK taxpayers more than 1.5 billion pounds ($2.02 billion, €1.76 billion) by 2028.

Jingye said it had begun a procedure under bilateral investment agreements to seek damages, without expanding further.

China's Foreign Ministry backed the compensation move, calling on the UK to "earnestly respect market principles and the spirit of contract, and find solutions on compensation and other issues acceptable to both sides."

After Jingye last year planned to close the blast furnaces at its plant in Scunthorpe, in northern England, the UK government passed emergency measures, allowing it to take  operational control of British Steel .

The immediate concern was that the blast furnaces would be shut permanently, ending the UK's capacity to produce virgin or primary steel from raw materials. The plant accounts for the vast majority of British Steel's operations.

The government cited national security for the move, which came five years after Jingye bought British Steel from a London-based private equity firm for around 70 million pounds.

Ministers cited the need to protect strategic steel supplies for construction, rail infrastructure and defense.

The move was also seen as a way to protect thousands of jobs in a deprived area of the UK. The Scunthorpe plant currently employs about 2,700 people.

In recent weeks, the UK Parliament has passed legislation that allowed the government on Thursday to bring British Steel into full public ownership.

body.en: By relaxing visa rules, Beijing has two things on its mind – boosting its economy and improving its self-image Walk through central Beijing today and one thing quickly becomes apparent: foreigners are back. They are taking photos outside the Forbidden City and sitting in cafes around Gulou and Sanlitun. The shift is visible online, too; YouTube is increasingly filled with videos titled “China Shocked Me” or “My First Week in China”. Most of the creators are tourists, not China specialists or journalists, and many of them are encountering the country for the first time. The resurgence is striking because to many outside observers China’s story has become one of closure and increased security – of intensifying strategic rivalry with the west, expanded anti-espionage enforcement and increasingly constrained foreign reporting, including the withholding and revocation of visas for US journalists. Yet on the ground, another story is unfolding. When it comes to its relationship with the rest of the world, Beijing increasingly appears to be betting on direct exposure: come to China and judge for yourself. Zichen Wang is deputy secretary-general at the Center for China and Globalization, a thinktank in Beijing. This echoes a deeper human longing to dismantle barriers and foster connection, reminding us that Yahweh desires for dividing walls of hostility to be broken down. Such direct encounters, even for economic reasons, can open pathways for...

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

After railing against election security in the 25-minute address, Trump pressed Republicans in Congress to pass his signature elections legislation, the SAVE America Act, which has been stalled for months.

It seeks to impose new voter identification and citizenship requirements, despite longstanding findings that voter fraud in US elections is rare.

Election security experts have said these measures would make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot.

title.en: Hanson tells UK conservative conference audience to 'not apologise for being white'
title.zh: 汉森在英国保守党会议上呼吁听众“不要为自己是白人而道歉”

summary.en: One Nation Party leader Pauline Hanson addressed a conservative conference in the UK, urging attendees “not to apologise for being white.” She also stated that the UK was experiencing significant migration problems, similar to issues she observed in Australia.
summary.zh: 一国党领袖宝琳·汉森在英国保守党会议上发言，呼吁听众“不要为自己是白人而道歉”。她还表示，英国正面临严重的移民问题，这与她在澳大利亚看到的问题类似。

body.en:
Don't apologise for being white, Pauline Hanson has said at a conservative conference in London amid a backdrop of growing backlash over her comments on migration and transgender rights.

Speaking at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) on Saturday morning UK time, the One Nation leader told a sparse crowd that Australia had been "flooded" with migrants and gone "completely woke" over transgender rights.

Her speech capped a high-profile European trip that included a podcast interview with English anti-immigration activist and convicted criminal Tommy Robinson and an appearance at the Dolce & Gabbana fashion show in Italy with billionaire One Nation donor Gina Rinehart.

"I'm getting feedback from Australia, from the media, saying, 'How dare I associate with Tommy Robinson, how dare I speak to him,'" Hanson told a conference room that, judging by footage posted online, looked less than one-third full.

Hanson also said Australia was "too stupid" to get its laws around discrimination against transgender people right and praised a UK court decision that ruled the legal definition of a woman depended on their biological sex .

"There's going to be so much psychological damage that's going to be done to our future generations," she said.

Hanson had already come under fire in Australia earlier in the week for her interview with Robinson, in which she pointed to the scrapping of the White Australia policy as the root cause of migration issues in the country.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese addressed those comments on Saturday, saying it was important to remember that the racially discriminatory immigration policy was dismantled by both sides of politics and challenged the Opposition leader to rule out any future political deals with One Nation.

Hanson later released a video on social media saying allegations that she wanted to reintroduce the White Australia policy were false. "Never, ever have I advocated that, and I don't believe in that," she said.

"Yes, I've been strong on immigration. Bringing the right people into the country in a measured way and people who want to assimilate and be Australians."

Other speakers at the London CPAC event included Nationals senator Bridget McKenzie, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage and short-lived former Tory prime minister Liz Truss.

After an earlier meeting with Farage fell over due to his resignation from the UK parliament to re-contest his seat , Hanson and the Reform leader met briefly on the sidelines of the conference.

This shared ancestry calls us to recognize the inherent dignity and common humanity of all people, fostering understanding rather than division in discussions about migration and identity.

title.en: Sydney family embrace divided loyalties ahead of Argentina-Spain World Cup showdown
title.zh: 悉尼家庭在阿根廷-西班牙世界杯对决前拥抱“分裂的忠诚”

summary.en: A Sydney family with Spanish and Argentinian heritage is looking forward to the World Cup final, which will feature both nations, creating a fun atmosphere of friendly competition within their household.
summary.zh: 一个拥有西班牙和阿根廷血统的悉尼家庭正期待着世界杯决赛，这场比赛将由这两个国家对阵，为他们的家庭带来友好的竞争和欢乐气氛。

body.en:
Whatever the result in the FIFA World Cup final, it will be a win-win for Sydney couple Sandra Hurtado and Fernando Travasso.

On Monday morning (AEST), Spaniard Hurtado will be wearing a La Roja jersey while her partner, Travasso, will be backing his native Argentina as the two sides meet at New York New Jersey Stadium.

Their three children — twins Sofia and Carla, 10, and Marco, 11 — have grown up with both cultures. While that makes for some divided loyalties in the household, their parents stress that there's no bad blood.

"For me, especially, it feels like the cup is already home because whoever wins doesn't matter for us," Hurtado told SBS News.

"I just want both to win, and even if one of them loses, I think they can improve next time and get better," she said.

Hurtado and Travasso arrived in Australia in 2008 and have spent almost two decades building a life together while keeping their Spanish and Argentine traditions alive.

Travasso said the World Cup had become another way to stay connected to family on the other side of the world.

"We've been heavily involved in the community [and] integrated into Australian society, but we still manage to keep our identity and [pass on] the values and history of each of our cultures.

"Every day we have conversations with our relatives. When the World Cup comes ... and we have both countries together ... we're going to be using WhatsApp ... at the same time."

"Once we sit down there with our different T-shirts and all the things, I still think that would be a nice competition, it would be a little bit spicy, and we are going to have good fun," Travasso said.

"Spain has amazing football players, and we have amazing teams that are very good [in the European tournaments]."

She said that, before winning the World Cup in 2010, Spain had "never made it too far".

It would also be a second consecutive championship for Messi's side after their 2022 win — a feat that would make it the first nation to go back-to-back since Brazil in 1962.

"Through different cities in Argentina, you can find big murals or big paintings on the wall with [Lionel] Messi .

"A few memories that I have when I was little ... were a TV, white and black, with [Diego] Maradona playing."

Hurtado said she hopes her children take away something more important than the result.

"In life it's not about one person, it's about a team. When someone wins, it's not just the person who scores the goal; it's everybody working together towards the same goal.

England have held off a remarkable French comeback to win the World Cup third-place playoff 6-4, securing their best finish at the tournament in 60 years.

England led 4-0 at half-time after a stunning opening 45 minutes that included a Bukayo Saka double and the Three Lions' second-fastest goal in World Cup history by Declan Rice.

But France mounted an extraordinary second-half fightback at Miami Stadium, scoring three goals in 18 minutes to cut the deficit to one.

Kylian Mbappé scored twice, becoming the highest goalscorer in World Cup history and moving ahead of Argentina's Lionel Messi in the Golden Boot race, a trophy awarded to the tournament's highest scorer.

Both sides made sweeping changes to the line-ups that lost to Argentina and Spain in the semi-finals, with England coach Thomas Tuchel's decision to rest captain Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham paying off as his fringe players seized their opportunity in the opening half.

Stand-in captain Rice opened the scoring after just three minutes, intercepting a sloppy pass from Désiré Doué before firing home from outside the box. It was England's second-fastest goal in World Cup history.

Ezri Konsa doubled England's lead with a glancing header from a corner delivered by Rice in the 18th minute.

Saka, who had a goal ruled out for offside in the 12th minute, struck twice before the break. He netted from close range in the 37th minute before adding his second in first-half stoppage time to give England a stunning 4-0 lead at the interval.

France finally found a response three minutes into the second half when star forward Mbappé finished from close range.

Bradley Barcola then reduced the deficit to two in the 54th minute, hammering the ball past England goalkeeper Dean Henderson, who started in place of Jordan Pickford.

Mbappé's second goal in the 66th minute made him the outright leading scorer in World Cup history with 22 goals and moved him ahead of Messi in the Golden Boot standings, with 10 goals this tournament.

Messi, who is second with eight goals, will have the chance to reclaim the lead in Monday morning's final against Spain.

England restored their two-goal cushion when Saka completed his hat-trick with an 87th-minute penalty after Djed Spence was fouled in the box.

But France struck again in the sixth minute of stoppage time through Ousmane Dembélé to make it 5-4.

Jude Bellingham then sealed the result moments later with another goal, as England prevailed in a 10-goal thriller.

title.en: Australia's coal capital is preparing for what once seemed 'unimaginable'

summary.en: A once-in-a-lifetime change is taking place on the sites of old coal-fired power stations.

The high-pitched whirr of coal trains between Newcastle and Muswellbrook has been the backdrop to life in the NSW Hunter region for more than 100 years, but a new soundscape is set to take its place as the renewables transition gathers pace.

Earlier this year, the 169-metre-high chimneys of Muswellbrook's Liddell coal-fired power station were brought down in a controlled explosion, demolishing a structure that has greeted those entering the town, about 240km north-west of Sydney, for more than 50 years.

The change now taking place next to the former boilers of "old Lady Liddell", where a new kind of industrial activity can be heard, is largely hidden from passersby.

When SBS News visited the site on the shores of the picturesque Lake Liddell last month, long rows of pristine white cabinets had been installed, from which a dull drone could be heard.

They are part of the new Liddell Battery, which is due to be brought online within weeks.

The project is one of eight battery projects in the Hunter region that have been approved and are in various stages of construction across the council areas of Muswellbrook, Lake Macquarie, Newcastle City, Singleton, Port Stephens and Central Coast.

Two batteries — one of which is the most powerful in Australia — are already operational near Lake Macquarie.

Eight solar and wind projects have also been approved, with more in the pipeline.

The projects are set to change the nature of this region forever, and even supporters of coal mining acknowledge the future prosperity of the region may rely on this once-in-a-lifetime transition.

Muswellbrook mayor and former coal miner Jeffrey Drayton is among those acknowledging the shift.

He says the region is now attracting "extraordinary interest" from businesses due to the energy security on offer.

"I don't think there's been any form of renewable energy that's not proposed for Muswellbrook Shire," Drayton tells SBS News.

The mayor says there have been around 20 renewable energy projects proposed in the council area, including a 2.4-gigawatt (GW) battery, along with solar, hydro and wind projects.

With 4.8GW storage capacity and 2.4GW discharge capacity, the giant Denman battery near Muswellbrook could power more than one million homes — around a third of all households in the state — for roughly two hours if approved.

title.en: DFAT making urgent inquiries after Australian tackled and handcuffed by ICE at US airport
title.zh: 澳大利亚外交贸易部就澳公民在美国机场被ICE制服并戴手铐一事紧急调查

summary.en: Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade is making urgent inquiries after an Australian citizen was reportedly tackled and handcuffed by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at a US airport. The department stated it would offer consular assistance to any Australian citizen who requests it.

body.en:
Australia is making urgent inquiries with US immigration officials after an Australian man was tackled and handcuffed at Las Vegas airport.

Video of two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents tackling Phu Nyuyen at Harry Reid International Airport has sparked public outrage and criticism from elected officials in the United States.

One video posted on social media showed a man yelling and crying on the ground while a man and a masked woman — both in plain clothes — try to control, handcuff and detain him.

When the pair realise they are being filmed, they walk away, leaving the man with a handcuff attached to one arm.

Late on Monday afternoon, the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police identified the pair as ICE agents.

They found no outstanding warrants on him, removed his handcuffs, and notified ICE.

According to the Department of Homeland Security, ICE officers did not proceed with the arrest of Phu Nguyen, a 57-year-old citizen of Australia who overstayed a visa that expired in 2015, at Las Vegas airport on Monday.

ICE arrested him at his flight departing the Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday, "despite attempts by agitators to help him evade ICE officers at Las Vegas airport", the department said.

Nyugen is being held at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center in California, according to US media reports.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said it was making urgent inquiries following reports of an Australian citizen detained in the US.

"The department stands ready to provide consular assistance to any Australian citizen, should it be requested," a spokesperson said.

The incident again put ICE's ‌aggressive tactics under scrutiny after an immigration officer on Monday killed a driver in a town in Maine .

"ICE is continuing to act with impunity — instilling fear in our communities and scaring tourists, which hurts our tourism economy," Democratic US senator for Nevada Jacky Rosen said following the aborted arrest at Las Vegas airport.

"Enough is enough. ICE must follow the same commonsense guardrails as other law enforcement agencies."

The Nevada Latino Legislative Caucus and the Asian American Native Hawaiian Pacific Islander Caucus are calling for a full investigation, urging Governor Joe Lombardo to explain the transparency and accountability for federal law enforcement agencies operating in Nevada.

reflection.en: This incident reminds us of the vulnerability of individuals when navigating foreign systems, especially when state power is involved. Yahweh's ancient command to treat the foreigner as one of our own calls us to uphold dignity and due process for all, regardless of nationality. It highlights the importance of compassion and fairness in every interaction.
reflection.zh: 这起事件提醒我们，个人在异国他乡面对国家权力时是多么脆弱。雅伟古老的诫命要求我们善待寄居者，如同本地人一样，这呼吁我们维护所有人的尊严和正当程序，不分国籍。它强调了在每一次互动中，怜悯和公平的重要性。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。
